assessment_type: Independent passage-backed engineering adjudication against holdout context and frozen rubric; not clinical validation

cases.claim: At 12 weeks HbA1c was 0.5 percentage points lower with intervention A than placebo; this does not establish within-group decline from baseline.
cases.source_passage: 240 adults were randomized to intervention A or placebo. At 12 weeks, HbA1c was 0.5 percentage points lower with intervention A than placebo. This was a between-group difference. The trial does not establish effects beyond 12 weeks.
cases.rationale: Both final claims preserve the between-group endpoint and avoid inferring a baseline rise or fall. The answer omits the 240-adult population required by the holdout. The visible uncertainty/limitations identify the record as demo evidence and do not imply real-world support.
cases.relevance: Directly answers whether the result is a within-group decrease or a between-group endpoint difference.
cases.coverage: Good coverage of the central question; required population qualifier is missing.
cases.attribution: Both claims cite the synthetic PubMed fixture. Demo disclosure appears in visible uncertainty/limitations, not in the main answer.
cases.followup_coherence: No follow-up history; concise and coherent.

cases.claim: The label reports different hypoglycemia percentages in different studies/populations and supplies no single overall risk number applicable to all ZITUVIMET users.
cases.source_passage: Label says adverse-reaction rates from clinical trials conducted under widely varying conditions cannot be directly compared. Separate table entries give add-on to glimepiride plus metformin (24 weeks) and add-on to insulin plus metformin (24 weeks), each with its own treatment and placebo groups.
cases.rationale: The no-pooled-number conclusion is cautious and consistent with separate trial-specific rates. However, the response does not explain the different background regimens and controls, nor preserve the required 24-week glimepiride/insulin add-on context. “No single overall risk number ... applies to all patients” is broader than the explicit source statement; safer wording is that the label reports separate regimen-specific trial rates and does not give a pooled rate.
missing_qualifiers: 24-week add-on to glimepiride plus metformin versus placebo control
24-week add-on to insulin plus metformin versus placebo control
Rates are trial-specific and are not directly comparable
cases.relevance: Answers whether there is one summary number but only partly answers why the label has different figures.
cases.coverage: Short and on topic, but does not state the regimen/control differences requested by the rubric.
cases.attribution: Cites the ZITUVIMET combination label; no rates are invented or assigned to metformin monotherapy.
cases.followup_coherence: No follow-up history. Visible uncertainty repeats the no-single-number limitation without adding useful regimen context.

cases.claim: Metformin is used to improve glycemic control in adults and children 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes; digestive adverse reactions and lactic acidosis warning are stated.
cases.source_passage: Metformin tablets are indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults and pediatric patients 10 years of age and older with type 2 diabetes. Common adverse reactions include diarrhea, nausea/vomiting, flatulence, asthenia, indigestion, abdominal discomfort, and headache; lactic acidosis appears as a warning.
cases.rationale: The plain-language answer preserves the age floor, type 2 diabetes population, digestive effects, and serious lactic-acidosis warning; it avoids fabricated efficacy magnitude. It omits the required adjunct-to-diet-and-exercise qualifier. Its visible uncertainty correctly says the label does not quantify benefit size.
missing_qualifiers: Used as an adjunct to diet and exercise
cases.relevance: Directly answers what metformin is for, who the indication covers, and downside in accessible language.
cases.coverage: Good concise benefit/risk coverage; diet/exercise use qualifier omitted.
cases.attribution: Claims cite the standalone metformin label. No demo disclosure applies to this real label excerpt.
cases.followup_coherence: No follow-up history; concise and understandable.

cases.claim: Intervention A as add-on to metformin produced a greater HbA1c and fasting glucose reduction versus placebo after 24 weeks; beyond-24-week benefit and mortality effect are not established.
cases.source_passage: Synthetic randomized trial in 180 adults with type 2 diabetes on stable metformin; intervention A or placebo was added for 24 weeks. Mortality was not measured. Effects beyond 24 weeks were not established.
cases.rationale: The answer preserves add-on status and 24-week duration and does not claim monotherapy, no effect, or unrelated safety findings. It says mortality effect is not established rather than stating the source-specific fact that mortality was not measured, a required qualifier for the question. The visible uncertainty/limitations disclose demo status.
missing_qualifiers: Mortality was not measured (rather than only saying effect is not established)
cases.relevance: Addresses both durability and survival questions without unrelated padding.
cases.coverage: Correct boundary language, but it omits the explicit mortality measurement status required by the holdout.
cases.attribution: Cites the synthetic PubMed source. Demo disclosure appears in visible uncertainty/limitations, not the main answer.
cases.followup_coherence: No follow-up history; concise and relevant.
